entries.title: Airport English: The Gate Changed
entries.hook: The first announcement names a gate. The second cancels it. Which gate survives?

turns.speaker: announcer
turns.text: Flight three-two gate twenty is now closing. Please proceed immediately.

turns.speaker: announcer
turns.text: Correction for flight three-two: use gate twenty-four instead. Gate twenty is closed.

turns.speaker: narrator
turns.text: The correction is the final instruction. When you hear correction, replace the old gate.

entries.prompt: Which gate should the passenger use?
entries.visualBrief: Bright modern airport departure hall with departure boards and two adult travellers looking up toward a gate sign, chest-up framing, hands below frame, silver blue and amber palette, no readable text.

entries.title: Stop Rereading: One Factual Review
entries.hook: The reread loop never finds a new mistake. It only finds the same one.

turns.speaker: narrator
turns.text: After you send a careful message, the loop offers one more read. But the words will not change.

turns.speaker: narrator
turns.text: So allow one factual review: spelling, names, dates. Then decide once.

turns.speaker: narrator
turns.text: When the loop restarts, say: I already checked the facts. The next step is sending, not rereading.

entries.prompt: What does the one factual review check?
entries.visualBrief: Calm night desk scene with an adult woman closing a laptop beside a warm lamp and a cup of tea, upper body only, hands below frame, muted teal and amber palette, no readable text.

entries.title: Airport Check-In: The Final Bag Rule
entries.hook: The agent first allows two bags, then changes the rule. How many go through?

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: For this fare, one cabin bag and one small personal item.

turns.speaker: passenger
turns.text: I have two cabin bags. May I take both?

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Not on this fare. The final rule is one cabin bag; the second must be checked.

entries.prompt: How many bags may the passenger carry on?
entries.visualBrief: Bright anime airport check-in counter with an adult traveller and an airline agent separated by a scale, upper bodies only, hands below frame, blue cream and orange palette, no readable text.

entries.title: Overthinking: Which Line Ends the Loop?
entries.hook: Three sentences sound supportive. Only one closes the reread loop.

turns.speaker: friend_a
turns.text: Maybe read it again, just to be safe.

turns.speaker: friend_b
turns.text: You already checked the facts, so the message is ready.

turns.speaker: narrator
turns.text: The first sentence feeds the loop. The second sentence ends it with the review you already did.

entries.visualBrief: Bright anime cafe window seat with two adult friends talking over phones placed face down, chest-up framing, hands mostly below frame, warm yellow and teal palette, no readable text.
